w: Villa Rufolo's layout dates from the 13th century, though most of what visitors see today came from an extensive 19th-century remodel. Set in the historic centre of Ravello above the Amalfi Coast, it faces straight onto the cathedral square, a quiet corner of a hill town built on medieval merchant wealth.
_facts: Initial layout dates from the 13th century
Extensively remodeled in the 19th century
Overlooks the cathedral square in Ravello

w: Villa Cimbrone dates from at least the 11th century, but its famous Terrazza dell'Infinito, the Terrace of Infinity, is a 20th-century addition: English aristocrat Ernest William Beckett, later Lord Grimthorpe, rebuilt the villa from salvaged fragments. It is now a hotel; its gardens remain open to the public.
s: Terrace of Infinity, rebuilt from salvaged fragments
_facts: Dates from at least the 11th century
Terrazza dell'Infinito rebuilt by Ernest William Beckett (Lord Grimthorpe) in the early 20th century
Built using salvaged architectural elements from elsewhere in Italy
Now a hotel; gardens open to the public

w: The name means Emerald Grotto. This sea cave at Conca dei Marini on the Amalfi Coast is partly inundated by the sea, its lower chamber flooded with seawater from the Tyrrhenian below. One of the coast's more curious natural landmarks, half cave, half saltwater pool, cut into the cliffs.
s: A sea cave half flooded by the Tyrrhenian
_facts: Name means "Emerald Grotto" in Italian
A cave partly inundated by the sea
Located in Conca dei Marini on the Amalfi Coast

w: The Diocesan Museum of Amalfi occupies the 9th-century Basilica del Crocifisso, beside Amalfi Cathedral on Via Salita Episcopio. It holds treasures of the Archdiocese of Amalfi-Cava de' Tirreni: church silver, vestments and relics, inside one of the town's oldest surviving religious buildings.
_facts: Housed in the 9th-century Basilica del Crocifisso (Basilica of the Crucifix)
Displays treasures of the Archdiocese of Amalfi-Cava de' Tirreni
Located on Via Salita Episcopio, next to Amalfi Cathedral

w: Built in the 11th century as the Palazzo D'Afflitto, this palace was destroyed by the Republic of Pisa, then lay abandoned until the mid-1500s. In 1893, hotelier Pantaleone Caruso rented five rooms and opened the Pensione Belvedere, named for its sea views. Guests since have included Virginia Woolf and Humphrey Bogart.
s: 11th-century palace turned hotel; guests: Woolf to Bogart
_facts: Built in the 11th century as the Palazzo D'Afflitto
Destroyed by the Republic of Pisa; rebuilt from the mid-1500s
Opened as the Pensione Belvedere in 1893 by Pantaleone Caruso
Guests included Virginia Woolf, Greta Garbo, Humphrey Bogart and Jackie Kennedy

w: Dating from the 11th or 12th century, this Romanesque church on Praiano's Via San Giovanni once served as the settlement's only parish, before growth brought eight more churches to town. Its maiolica floor, tiled with flora and fauna, survives in remarkable condition. First documented in a 1296 bill of sale.
s: Praiano's original church, floored in painted maiolica
_facts: Romanesque church dating from the 11th-12th centuries
Well-preserved maiolica tiled floor with flora and fauna motifs
Pipe organ built by Neapolitan organ masters
First documented in a 1296 bill of sale; was once the area's only church
